clauses.claim: ASME B31.1 para 137 is titled "Pressure Tests" (leak testing requirements for power piping)

votes.evidence:
Several independent secondary sources agree that ASME B31.1 para 137 is titled "Pressure Tests" (Chapter VI, Inspection, Examination, and Testing). I could not open a primary ASME table of contents. ASME hosts the B31.1-2022 one at asme.org/getmedia/23f87c07-13fa-4fd6-a24d-9ab09cc05012/b31-1_2022_toc.pdf, but the egress proxy blocked it, along with studylib, accuristech, energy-steel and standardsmichigan.
(1) Search snippets of the ASME B31.1-2016 public review draft (standardsmichigan.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/Proposed-Revision-of-B31.X-Power-Piping-Public-Review-Draft-2346.pdf) show the heading "137 PRESSURE TESTS". 137.1 General Requirements opens with subassemblies and leak-tightness testing.
(2) An older B31.1 NRC adoption notice (nrc.gov/docs/ML0314/ML031470592.pdf) lists "Pressure Tests" with General Requirements, Preparation for Testing, Hydrostatic, Pneumatic and Mass-Spectrometer/Halide testing. So the numbering and title go back to at least the 1990s.
(3) An Eng-Tips thread quotes the code: "137.3.2 Nonboiler External Piping ... hydrostatically tested in accordance with para. 137.4 ... leak tested in accordance with para. 137.5, 137.6, or 137.7" (eng-tips.com/threads/b31-1-hydro-vs-rt-exam.271105). The same thread discusses the B31.1-2020 addition after 137.3.2 (137.8 NDE alternative), so para 137 still holds pressure testing in 2020.
(4) 46 CFR 56.97-1 is titled "General (replaces 137)" and says its pressure-test rules apply "in lieu of 137 of ASME B31.1" (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/46/56.97-1).
(5) NATA accreditation scopes cite B31.1 137.4 for hydrostatic and 137.5 for pneumatic testing, and wermac.org cites 137.7.1 for initial service testing.
Caveats: B31.1 calls this a "pressure test" whose purpose is to show leak tightness, so "leak testing requirements" is a fair description. The required test type (hydrostatic, pneumatic or initial service) is set in 137.3 to 137.7 and varies by boiler external versus nonboiler external piping. B31.1-2020/2022 added an NDE alternative to hydrotesting for some piping. Sources such as industrialmonitordirect.com/araner that cite "345.x" for B31.1 are mixing in B31.3 numbering and should be ignored.

The search results agree that ASME B31.1 Chapter VI (Inspection, Examination, and Testing) para. 137 is titled "Pressure Tests" and covers leak-tightness testing of power piping. I could only see this through search-result summaries: direct fetches of asme.org, eng-tips, ecfr/cornell and energy-steel.com were blocked by the sandbox proxy (403 / DNS failure), so I could not open the documents myself.

Evidence:
(1) A reproduction of the B31.1 code on energy-steel.com (uploaded 2025-03) lists "137 · Pressure Tests" in its table of contents: https://energy-steel.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/ASME-B31.1.pdf
(2) An NRC copy of the B31.1 adoption notice lists "Pressure Tests", "Preparation for Testing" and "Initial Service Testing" under Inspection, Examination, and Testing: https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML0314/ML031470592.pdf
(3) An eng-tips thread quotes para. 137.1.1: pressure testing "to ensure leak tightness" is acceptable for finding leaks in piping subassemblies. It also quotes 136.4.1: welds "shall be judged acceptable if they meet ... the pressure test requirements specified in para. 137": https://www.eng-tips.com/threads/is-all-the-piping-subject-to-pressure-test-by-b31-1.332581/
(4) The ASME B31.1 product page for the 2024 edition lists a revision to para. 137.2.1, Exposure of Joints: joints must be uncoated "during a pressure test" unless the owner allows otherwise. This shows para. 137 is still the pressure-test paragraph in the current edition: https://www.asme.org/codes-standards/find-codes-standards/b31-1-power-piping
(5) ABSA AB-519 quotes 137.4.6(c): closure welds joining systems "successfully tested under para. 137": https://www.absa.ca/media/1506/ab-519_alternative_test_methods_procedure_requirements.pdf
(6) 46 CFR Subpart 56.97 "Pressure Tests" replaces B31.1 para. 137 for USCG piping, and its text speaks of a "hydrostatic leak test" to demonstrate leak tightness: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-46/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-56/subpart-56.97
Secondary sources also cite the subparagraphs 137.1.4 (max stress during test), 137.3.1/137.3.2 (BEP/NBEP), 137.4 (hydrostatic), 137.5 (pneumatic, incl. 137.5.5) and 137.7 (initial service).

Caveats for the field tool:
(a) Para. 137 supports the "leak test done" part of the checkpoint. I found nothing showing that para. 137 itself requires a signed test record; that part may come from owner, jurisdiction or BEP/Section I documentation rules, so do not present para. 137 as the source of the "record signed" requirement.
(b) A vendor summary of B31.1-2022 says Chapter VI now allows NDE as an alternative to hydrostatic testing for NBEP, and initial service testing is permitted in some cases. "Leak test done" can therefore legitimately mean an alternative method under para. 137, not only a hydrotest.
(c) Some web sources wrongly cite "345" for B31.1. That is B31.3 numbering and should not be mixed in.

clauses.claim: ASME B31.3 para 345 is titled "Testing" (leak test requirements), and para 345.3.1 requires joints (incl. welds and bonds) to be left exposed/uninsulated for examination during the leak test

votes.evidence:
Several independent secondary sources agree on the paragraph number, title and content. I could not open the ASME primary text: WebFetch failed DNS on every domain and the proxy blocked curl, so all of this comes from WebSearch result summaries.

(1) Para 345 "Testing" is the B31.3 leak-test paragraph. Its subparagraphs are 345.1 Required Leak Test, 345.2 General Requirements, 345.3 Preparation for Leak Test, 345.4 Hydrostatic, 345.5 Pneumatic, 345.6 Hydrostatic-Pneumatic, 345.7 Initial Service, 345.8 Sensitive and 345.9 Alternative. Sources: petrosync.com/blog/?p=2755; safteng.net/preparing-for-a-piping-leak-test-b31-3/; app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=248641, which quotes the 2011 opening of 345.1, "Prior to initial operation... each piping system shall be tested to ensure tightness."

(2) 345.3.1 is titled "Joints Exposed." Quoted text: "All joints, welds (including structural attachment welds to pressure-containing components), and bonds shall be left uninsulated and exposed for examination during leak testing, except that joints previously tested in accordance with this Code may be insulated or covered. All joints may be primed and painted prior to leak testing unless a sensitive leak test (para. 345.8) is required." Sources: AWS forum app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?tid=18721; safteng.net; eng-tips thread "B31.3 345.3.1 (b) Joints Exposed Question" (eng-tips.com/threads/b31-3-345-3-1-b-joints-exposed-question.459532/); eng-tips qid=522796; qualityinspectionforms.com/weld-codes-standards/asme-b313-pressure-testing-painted-welds.

(3) The 2016 edition added an exception. Per the Becht article "ASME B31.3 – Substantive Changes in the 2016 Edition" (becht.com/becht-blog/entry/asme-b31-3-substantive-changes-in-the-2016-edition/) and whatispiping.com/asme-b-31-3-2016-vs-asme-b-31-3-2014/: at the owner's option, joints in Category D fluid service that get a hydrostatic or initial service leak test may be insulated and have weather sheathing installed before the test. The test period should then be lengthened. Recent editions split 345.3.1 into lettered subparagraphs; the eng-tips thread cites 345.3.1(b), and qualityinspectionforms cites (b) for previously tested joints and (c) for Category D. I could not confirm the exact (a) to (d) lettering for 2016 to 2022.

(4) The older numbering was 331.3 (1983 interpretation) and later 337.3, before the move to 345. This does not affect the 2016 to 2022 editions.

Caveat for the tool: the "Joints covered before test" defect is a correct cite of 345.3.1. It is not a violation where the joints were tested earlier under the Code (for example, shop-tested spools), or where the owner allowed insulation on Category D piping. Cite "345.3.1" without a letter unless the edition is checked.

Both parts of the claim hold up. The para 345 title and the text of 345.3.1 are confirmed by secondary sources. WebFetch and curl could not reach any site from this environment (DNS and proxy errors), so the evidence comes from WebSearch result excerpts, not full pages.

(1) Title: A forum post quoting the 2011 edition reproduces the heading as "345 TESTING  345.1 Required Leak Test  Prior to initial operation, and after completion of the applicable examinations required by para. ..." Other headings quoted on forums match: 345.2.6 "Repairs or Additions After Leak Testing" and 345.2.7 test records. Sources: https://www.scribd.com/document/528626921/15243, https://app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=248641

(2) 345.3.1 "Joints Exposed": search excerpts reproduce the B31.3-2004 and 2006 wording: "All joints, welds (including structural attachment welds to pressure-containing components), and bonds shall be left uninsulated and exposed for examination during leak testing, except that joints previously tested in accordance with this Code may be insulated or covered." The paragraph also allows joints to be primed and painted before the test, except when a sensitive leak test (345.8) is required. Sources: https://safteng.net/preparing-for-a-piping-leak-test-b31-3/, https://www.scribd.com/document/488587822/piping-testing, https://cstools.asme.org/csconnect/FileUpload.cfm?View=yes&ID=28740 (Interpretation 22-09, which concerns para 345.3.1 "Joints Exposed"), and ASME Interpretation 5-10 on previously tested joints. An ASME interpretation also cites "para. 345.2.2(a) and 345.3.1" for visual observation of joints during leak tests, in the jacketed-piping exception.

(3) Recent editions: in the 2016 and later editions the paragraph is split into lettered subparagraphs. An Eng-Tips thread is titled "B31.3 345.3.1 (b) Joints Exposed Question" (https://www.eng-tips.com/threads/b31-3-345-3-1-b-joints-exposed-question.459532/). Becht and ANSI summaries of the 2016 changes say an owner-permitted option was added to insulate or cover joints in Category D fluid service piping during leak testing, with a longer test period to be considered. The core requirement stays in 345.3.1 (in later editions, 345.3.1(a)), so citing "345.3.1" is still correct.

Caveats for the tool text:
(a) The rule has exceptions: joints previously tested under the Code, and since 2016, Category D piping at the owner's option.
(b) "Covered" means insulated or covered. Primer and paint are allowed before the test unless a sensitive leak test is required, so do not flag painted joints under this clause.
(c) The "record signed" part of the checkpoint comes from 345.2.7 (Test Records), not 345.3.1. Para 345 as a whole fits the "Leak test done" checkpoint.

I could not read the current (2022 or 2024) edition directly, so the exact lettering of the subparagraphs in the newest edition is not verified.

clauses.claim: ASME B31.1 para 136 is titled "Inspection and Examination"

votes.evidence:
The number and title are correct. ASME B31.1 Chapter VI is "Inspection, Examination, and Testing". Para 136 is "Inspection and Examination" and para 137 is "Pressure Tests". Sources:
(1) A search snippet from a copy of the B31.1-2022 code (front matter "Date of Issuance: October 10, 2022"; https://energy-steel.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/ASME-B31.1.pdf) lists "136 · Inspection and Examination" and "137 · Pressure Tests". Its Summary of Changes marks 136.3.2 as "Revised in its entirety", which means para 136 is still in use in 2022.
(2) A Michigan LARA notice on B31.1 non-boiler external piping (https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/bcc/sections/boiler-unit/division/notice-to-owners-and-installers-of-b31-1-non-boiler-external-pipe) cites "2010 ... B31.1, Chapter VI, 136 Inspection and Examination". It quotes 136.1.1 and 136.1.4(A).
(3) Minnesota rule 5230.0305 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/minnesota/Minn-R-5230-0305) and the MN DLI 2022 draft (https://www.dli.mn.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/SR46_30_draft043622.pdf) adopt the B31.1 2016/2020 editions. They amend 136.1 through 136.3.2 and refer to 136.4.2 through 136.4.6, so the para 136 structure exists in the 2016 and 2020 editions.
(4) Secondary NDE sources (atlantisndt.com, weldfabworld.com) cite 136.1/136.2 (inspection), 136.3 (examination), 136.4.2 (visual) and Table 136.4.1-1, which matches recent-edition numbering.
Together these cover 2010 through 2022 with the same number and title.
Limits: I could not open the ASME TOC PDF or the code copy directly because the network blocked the downloads. The 2022 confirmation comes from search-result excerpts of that PDF, not a direct read.
On how it is used: para 136 fits a general "Weld/NDE records complete" checkpoint because it covers owner inspection and the required weld examination (136.4 and Table 136.4.1-1). Weld repair rules are in para 127.4.11, so if the tool cites repairs specifically it should not attribute them to 136.

I could not read the ASME text itself. WebFetch and curl to the Michigan, Minnesota, studylib and Cornell pages all failed on DNS or a proxy 403, so what follows comes from search-result excerpts and what I already knew. Several secondary sources agree: B31.1 Chapter VI is "Inspection, Examination, and Testing", para 136 is "Inspection and Examination", and para 137 is "Pressure Tests". The 136 subparagraphs match those headings. 136.1 is Inspection: the Michigan LARA notice on the 2010 edition quotes 136.1.1, "inspection is the responsibility of the Owner and may be performed by employees of the Owner or a party authorized by the Owner", and also 136.1.4(A), the Owner's Inspector. 136.3 is Examination: an AWS forum post quoting the 2007 edition gives 136.3.1, "Examination denotes the functions performed by the manufacturer, fabricator, erector, or a party authorized by the Owner", including VT, RT, UT, ET, PT and MT. 136.4 covers examination methods and acceptance standards (Table 136.4, and 136.4.2 for visual per Section V Article 9). Minnesota rule 5230.0305 and the SR46 draft rule both refer to "section 136" and to 136.4.2 through 136.4.6. Sources: michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/bcc/sections/boiler-unit/division/notice-to-owners-and-installers-of-b31-1-non-boiler-external-pipe; app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=160549; app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?tid=22194; revisor.mn.gov/rules/pdf/5230.0305/2014-01-18; dli.mn.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/SR46_30_draft043622.pdf. The clause number and title are confirmed. How well it fits the checkpoint is weaker. Para 136 is about inspection and examination of welds (including inspection before initial operation for compliance with examination requirements), so it works as a general pointer for "Weld/NDE records complete". It does not say "records complete" or "no open repairs" itself. Weld repair is para 127.4.11, and an AWS forum user (2007 edition) says B31.1 has no explicit requirement for inspection or NDE records. Two more caveats: Minnesota deletes para 136 for some steam and heating piping, and 2022 and later editions changed Chapter VI (adding NDE as an alternative to hydrotest for nonboiler external piping). I found nothing showing para 136 was renumbered, but I did not see the 2022 or 2024 table of contents. It is fine to cite it as "para 136 Inspection and Examination". Do not present it as the requirement for record completeness or repair closure. Pairing it with 127.4.11 for repairs would be more accurate.

The claim is right: ASME B31.3 para 341 is titled "Examination". It sits in Chapter VI, "Inspection, Examination, and Testing". That chapter has kept the same headings across editions: 340 Inspection, 341 Examination, 342 Examination Personnel, 343 Examination Procedures, 344 Types of Examination, 345 Testing, 346 Records.

Sources found through web search (search snippets and summaries only; every direct fetch failed with DNS/proxy errors, so I did not open any PDF myself):
- ASME's official table of contents PDFs for B31.3-2022 (https://www.asme.org/getmedia/2d6bec7b-1177-4ee1-82ea-e5d5a86abab7/B31-3_2022_ToC.pdf) and B31.3-2020 (https://www.asme.org/wwwasmeorg/media/Codes-Standards/Find-Codes/B31-3_Process-Piping-2020-ToC.pdf). Both came up for a search on "341 Examination" / "344 Types of Examination" / "346 Records" in Chapter VI. I could not open them to quote the text.
- Studylib copies of B31.3-2018, 2020 and 2024 (https://studylib.net/doc/27749867/b31-3-2018, https://studylib.net/doc/27169758/asme-b31.3-2020-process-piping--2-, https://studylib.net/doc/27696061/asme-b31.3-2024). The search summary said they show the same 340-346 heading sequence, with 341 Examination.
- ANSI preview of B31.3-2006 (https://webstore.ansi.org/preview-pages/ASME/preview_ASME+B31.3-2006.pdf) and the Accuristech preview (https://store.accuristech.com/tia/products/preview/1287406) also show this sequence, per the search summary.
- ASME B31.3 Interpretations Vol. 21 (https://cstools.asme.org/csconnect/FileUpload.cfm?View=yes&ID=26668) has an index entry "Para. 341, Examination", with subparagraphs 341.3.1(a) and 341.4. A PHMSA interpretation (https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/sites/phmsa.dot.gov/files/docs/standards-rulemaking/pipeline/interpretations/75986/ch-iv-pi-21-0009-10-07-2021-part193-2303.pdf) cites 341.4.1(b)(1) random examination under the 2020-era numbering.

This matches what I already knew: the 341 numbering and title have not changed from 2016 through 2022.

Advisory note for the checkpoint "Weld/NDE records complete, no open repairs": 341 covers the examination requirements, including what to do about defects and repairs (341.3.3 Defective Components and Workmanship) and progressive sampling (341.3.4). Record retention is in 346 "Records". The tool could cite 341 together with 346 if it wants to cover the records part. I have not confirmed the exact subparagraph titles beyond the snippets above.

The title is correct. In ASME B31.3, Chapter VI "Inspection, Examination, and Testing" is numbered 340 Inspection, 341 Examination, 342 Examination Personnel, 343 Examination Procedures, 344 Types of Examination, 345 Testing, 346 Records. The ANSI webstore preview of the B31.3-2006 table of contents lists "Chapter VI Inspection, Examination, and Testing; 340 Inspection; 341 Examination" (https://webstore.ansi.org/preview-pages/ASME/preview_ASME+B31.3-2006.pdf). A Docsity listing of the 2004 edition shows the same 340-346 structure (https://www.docsity.com/pt/docs/asme-b31-3-2004/4762131/). The numbering has been stable from about 2004 into current editions, and secondary sources citing the 2006 and 2010 editions use the same 341.x and 346.x numbers. I could not open the primary PDFs: WebFetch and curl were blocked by DNS and the proxy. So this rests on search-result excerpts of the table of contents, which several sources agree on.

Fit to the checkpoint: paragraph 341 partly supports it.
- **"No open repairs":** this part fits 341. Para 341.3.3 "Defective Components and Workmanship" is quoted on the AWS forum as: "An examined item with one or more defects ... shall be repaired or replaced; and the new work shall be reexamined by the same methods, to the same extent, and by the same acceptance criteria as required for the original work." ASME/AWS-cited Interpretation 22-04 (B31.3-2006) also cites para 341.3.3 for re-examining repaired welds (https://app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?tid=22089, https://eng-tips.com/threads/weld-repair-asme-b31-3.515545). Para 341.3.4, progressive sampling, also covers repairing until accepted.
- **"Records complete":** this part is not in 341. It belongs to para 346 "Records". 346.2 covers responsibility for preparing the records the Code requires. 346.3 covers retention of examination procedures and examiner qualification records, at least 5 years, as cited by the LANL manual for the 2010 edition (https://engstandards.lanl.gov/esm/pressure_safety/ADMIN-1-2-R0.pdf).

Recommendation: keep "B31.3 para 341 Examination", which is not misleading. Better still, cite "341 (incl. 341.3.3)" for repairs and add "346 Records" for record completeness. The 346 sub-paragraph wording and retention details should be checked against the edition the project is contracted to.

clauses.claim: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.4 (Gaskets) says no more than one gasket shall be used between contact faces in assembling a flanged joint

votes.evidence:
The claim is correct. ASME B31.3 para 335.2.4 is titled "Gaskets" and reads: "No more than one gasket shall be used between contact faces in assembling a flanged joint." This is the same wording given in the claim.

Sources:
- safteng.net reproduces B31.3 para 335, "Assembly and Erection of Flanged Joints", in two places: https://safteng.net/asme-b31-3-335-assembly-and-erection-of-flanged-joints/ and https://safteng.net/?p=12004
- That reproduction lists the 335.2 (Flanged Joints) sub-paragraphs in order: 335.2.1 Preparation for Assembly, 335.2.2 Bolting Torque, 335.2.3 Bolt Length, 335.2.4 Gaskets (the text above) and 335.2.5 Flanged Joint Assembly. 335.2.5 refers to ASME PCC-1 and BPVC Sec VIII Div 1 Nonmandatory Appendix S, which suggests the reproduction is from a recent edition, not an old one.
- A Brainscape B31.3 "Fabrication, Assembly and Erection" flashcard set has the same sentence: https://brainscape.com/flashcards/b313-fabrication-assembly-and-erection-2834931/packs/4152407
- A Little P.Eng post on B31.3 flanged-joint limitations also came up for the exact quote: https://www.littlepeng.com/single-post/2017/09/14/asme-b313-limitations-on-flanged-joints
- This also matches my own knowledge: the number and title of 335.2.4 have not changed across B31.3 editions, including 2016 through 2022.

Limits on this check:
- These are all secondary sources. Every direct page fetch was blocked by DNS or the proxy, so the text comes from search-result extracts, not from loading the pages.
- I could not see an official ASME table of contents. A studylib copy of B31.3-2020 turned up in search but could not be fetched.
- I found no ASME interpretation that changes or adds exceptions to this paragraph.
- The rule is about assembly (only one gasket between contact faces), so it fits the "Single gasket only" checkpoint.

The clause says what the claim says, and citing it beside "Single gasket only" is not misleading. A third-party reproduction of B31.3 Section 335 on safteng.net (https://safteng.net/asme-b31-3-335-assembly-and-erection-of-flanged-joints/ and https://safteng.net/?p=12004) quotes para 335.2.4 "Gaskets" word for word: "No more than one gasket shall be used between contact faces in assembling a flanged joint." Search results quote the paragraphs around it in the same numbering: 335.2.3 Bolt Length ("Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut") and 335.2.5 Flanged Joint Assembly. 335.2.5 says assembly requirements and flanged joint assembler qualifications "shall be considered in the engineering design" and points to ASME PCC-1 and BPVC Section VIII Div 1 Nonmandatory Appendix S. That 335.2.5 wording appears only in recent editions (about 2018 onward), so the numbering matches current editions. API 570/B31.3 exam-prep material (a slideshare practice set, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/api-570-b313-qustionpdf/258047715) has an answer that says two gaskets are unacceptable and the joint must take only one. This also matches my own knowledge: the 335.2.4 text has stayed the same across many editions. Limits: I could not open the ASME original or the 2022 table of contents (WebFetch and curl to asme.org and safteng.net were blocked), so the wording comes from a secondary reproduction confirmed through search snippets. I found no official ASME interpretation on 335.2.4. Nuance for the field tool: the rule is one gasket per pair of contact faces. A joint with an inserted plate, such as a spectacle blind or spacer, has two pairs of contact faces and can properly have one gasket on each side, so the checkpoint should read "one gasket per pair of contact faces (no stacked gaskets)".

clauses.claim: ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 (Bolt Length) says bolts should extend completely through their nuts, and (in common editions) that bolts failing to do so are considered acceptably engaged if the lack of complete engagement is not more than one thread

votes.correction: Keep the number and title, ASME B31.3 para 335.2.3 "Bolt Length", but change the content for recent editions. Secondary quotes of the 2020 edition give the text as: "Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut." The "should extend completely through their nuts... acceptably engaged if the lack of complete engagement is not more than one thread" wording belongs to older editions (2012 and earlier, per forum commentary). It should not be cited as 2016-2022 content. Suggested checkpoint text: "Studs/bolts: complete thread engagement for full nut depth (B31.3 335.2.3, verify edition)."
votes.evidence:
The number and title are confirmed by several secondary sources that list 335.2.3 "Bolt Length" under 335.2 Flanged Joints in B31.3, next to 335.2.4 Gaskets. The ASME 2022 table of contents lists Section 335 Assembly and Erection: https://www.asme.org/getmedia/2d6bec7b-1177-4ee1-82ea-e5d5a86abab7/B31-3_2022_ToC.pdf (I could not open it; the proxy blocked it).

The content conflicts by edition:
(1) An Eng-Tips thread, https://www.eng-tips.com/threads/thread-engagement.509819/ , as seen in search-result excerpts, quotes "ASME B31.3 2020, 335.2.3 Bolt Length: Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut". The same thread says the one-thread-short allowance applied to "2012 and older" editions.
(2) safteng.net, https://safteng.net/asme-b31-3-335-assembly-and-erection-of-flanged-joints/ , quotes the same newer 335.2.3 wording next to 335.2.4 Gaskets ("No more than one gasket...").
(3) The one-thread wording appears only in older or undated secondary sources: Brainscape flashcards, a SlideShare practice-question deck, a Portland Bolt FAQ, a Mike Holt forum post, a 2008 materials-welding blog post, and a forum reference to Interpretation 17-20 on the 1998 addenda.

So the claim that common or recent editions keep the one-thread allowance looks outdated for B31.3-2016 to 2022. The newer wording is confirmed for 2020. I could not find out whether the change came in 2014 or 2016; whatispiping's summaries of the 2016 and 2018 changes did not turn up a 335.2.3 entry. All fetches of primary or full-text sources (ASME, eng-tips, ssmalloys B31.3-2018 PDF, slideshare, brainscape) failed through the proxy, so this rests on search-result excerpts, not the code text.

The "fully through nut" checkpoint fits the newer requirement. The one-thread tolerance should not be cited. Mark it "verify clause/edition" unless the project edition is confirmed.

votes.correction: The clause number and title are right: ASME B31.3 para. 335.2.3 "Bolt Length". The content is out of date. The 2016 edition removed the one-thread allowance. The 2016 and later text (2020 wording as quoted secondhand) reads: "Bolts shall extend through their nuts such that there is complete thread engagement for the full depth of the nut." Suggested citation for the checkpoints: "B31.3 335.2.3 (2016+): bolts shall extend through nuts with complete thread engagement for full nut depth. The old 'not more than one thread short' allowance applies only to pre-2016 editions." Otherwise show "verify clause/edition".
votes.evidence:

clauses.claim: ASME B31.3 para 322.6.1 is titled "Stop Valves in Pressure Relief Piping" and requires stop valves between protected equipment and its relief device (or on discharge) to be locked/sealed open (or otherwise controlled) per the code conditions

votes.evidence:
The number and title are confirmed by secondary sources. I could not fetch the primary ASME text: WebFetch and curl were blocked by DNS/proxy, so all confirmation comes from search-result excerpts.

Sources that confirm it:
(1) SAFTENG has an article titled "Stop Valves in Pressure Relief Piping (ASME B31.3)" that discusses B31.3-2018 (https://safteng.net/stop-valves-in-pressure-relief-piping-asme-b31-3/). Its full text is behind a paywall.
(2) TSASK (Saskatchewan) publishes "Pressure relief path stop valve control program manual requirements". It asks for the applied code clause for each relief-path stop valve and lists B31.3 322.6.1(a), 322.6.1(b) and 322.6.1(c) (https://www.tsask.ca/publication/pressure-relief-path-stop-valve-control-program-manual-requirements/).
(3) A LittlePEng note on B31.3 overpressure protection says "block valves are permitted in the inlet and discharge lines to the relief valve, with certain limitations ... outlined in para. 322.6.1". It places this under 322.6 Pressure Relieving Systems (https://www.littlepeng.com/amp/2017/08/03/asme-b313-over-pressure-protection).
(4) An Eng-Tips thread places 322.6.3 next to these paragraphs as the reference to ASME VIII/XIII (https://www.eng-tips.com/viewthread.cfm?qid=499443). This matches the 322.6 structure: 322.6.1 stop valves, 322.6.2 discharge piping, 322.6.3 devices.

What the paragraph says, from recall checked against the parallel B31.12 IP-7.2.1 text that SAFTENG quotes: stop valves between protected piping and its relief device, or between the device and the point of discharge, must meet (a) and either (b) or (c).
- (a) Full-area valves are allowed. Less-than-full-area valves are allowed only if the extra pressure drop does not reduce relieving capacity or affect how the device works.
- (b) The valves must be built or positively controlled so that closing the most block valves possible at one time does not drop capacity below what is required.
- (c) Alternatively, the valves must be built and arranged so they can be locked or sealed in either the open or closed position. Paragraph (c) refers to Appendix F, F322.6.

This paragraph has been in B31.3 from well before 2016 through 2022.

Caveat on the wording: the code does not literally require every such valve to be "locked open". It requires either capacity-preserving control under (b), or valves that can be locked or sealed open or closed under (c). Keeping them LO/CSO during operation is how the code is applied, through Appendix F (nonmandatory), API 520/521 and owner or jurisdictional programs. The claim's phrase "locked/sealed open (or otherwise controlled) per the code conditions" is an acceptable paraphrase, and citing 322.6.1 for the "PSV block valves secured per P&ID (LO/CSO)" checkpoint fits. This applies to B31.3 piping only. Valves protecting pressure vessels fall under ASME VIII/XIII.

Paragraph number and title are corroborated by secondary sources, but I could not get the verbatim B31.3 text. WebFetch and curl were blocked by the egress proxy for every host I tried (safteng.net, eng-tips.com, littlepeng.com, tsask.ca, tn.gov, archive.org, scribd, studylib). Only search-result snippets were available.

Secondary confirmation found:
(1) safteng.net has an article titled "Stop Valves in Pressure Relief Piping (ASME B31.3)" (https://safteng.net/stop-valves-in-pressure-relief-piping-asme-b31-3/). It discusses B31.3-2018 allowing these stop valves while equipment is in operation. The article itself is paywalled.
(2) littlepeng.com (https://www.littlepeng.com/single-post/2017/08/03/ASME-B313-Over-Pressure-protection) says "block valves are permitted in the inlet and discharge lines to the relief valve, with certain limitations. These requirements are outlined in para. 322.6.1."
(3) An eng-tips thread (https://www.eng-tips.com/threads/hi-all-can-someone-tell-me-as-t.198584/) points to "section 322.6.1 of ASME B31.3" for block valves in pressure relief piping.
(4) The Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK) Pressure Relief Path Stop Valve Control Program manual requirements (https://api.tsask.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/IP-2016-07-08_-_PRP_SVC_Program_Manual_Requirements.pdf) cites "322.6.1(a), 322.6.1(b), or 322.6.1(c)". It also requires the mechanical locking elements to be described (padlock, lead seals, etc.).
(5) The sister code B31.12, para IP-7.2.1, was quoted in a search snippet (https://safteng.net/add-asme-b31-12-to-the-list-allowing-intervening-valves-in-the-prv-path/). The snippet gives: "so constructed or positively controlled that the closing of the maximum number of block valves possible at one time will not reduce the pressure relieving capacity provided by the unaffected relieving devices below the required relieving capacity", and "As an alternative to (c) above, stop valves shall be so constructed and arranged that they can be locked or sealed in either the open or closed position." This matches what I recall of B31.3 322.6.1, apart from the subparagraph lettering.

From memory, not verified verbatim: B31.3 322.6.1 says stop valves between the protected piping and its relief device, or between the device and the point of discharge, shall meet (a) and either (b) or (c).
- (a) Full-area stop valves are allowed, with conditions on reduced-area valves.
- (b) Valves are constructed or positively controlled so that closing the maximum number of block valves at one time does not reduce relieving capacity below what is required.
- (c) As an alternative to (b), valves are constructed and arranged so they can be locked or sealed in either the open or closed position. This subparagraph refers to Appendix F, para F322.6.
F322.6 is nonmandatory ("should") guidance. It says an authorized person attends while a valve is closed and locks or seals it open before leaving.

Nuance for the claim: 322.6.1 does not itself say "must be locked/sealed open". It requires lock/seal capability in either position, as an alternative to positive capacity control. The "secured open" practice is in F322.6. The claim's wording "(or otherwise controlled) per the code conditions" covers this well enough. Next to a checkpoint that reads "secured per P&ID (LO/CSO)", the citation is the right governing paragraph and is not misleading.

Suggested display text: "B31.3 322.6.1 (see also App. F, F322.6)". I am not aware of renumbering in the 2018 to 2024 editions, but I could not confirm the current-edition text.

clauses.claim: API 650 Section 10.1 is titled "Nameplates" (tank nameplate requirements) in the 12th/13th edition

votes.evidence:
The numbering and title hold up. In API 650 from the 11th edition (2007) onward, Section 10 is "Marking" and 10.1 is "Nameplates". Note that Section 10 is titled "Marking", not "Nameplates". 10.1.1 requires a nameplate similar to Figure 10.1 (10-1 in older editions), with letters and numerals at least 4 mm (5/32 in.) high. 10.1.2 covers where it goes: attached to the shell next to a manhole or its reinforcing plate. 10.1.3 and 10.1.4 cover the fabricator and erector names. 10.2 is Division of Responsibility and 10.3 is Certification (Figure 10.2).

Sources (snippets from search results; the network proxy blocked opening any full documents):
(1) API's own 12th-edition errata (July 2013, api.org/~/media/files/certification/monogram-apiqr/0_api-monogram-apiqr/advisories-updates/addenda-errata/api_650_12th-edition_errata-1_july-2013.pdf). Its snippet says Annex M nameplate marking adds "M" to the information required by 10.1.1, and puts the maximum design temperature in the space shown in Figure 10.1. That ties 10.1.1 to the nameplate in the 12th edition.
(2) A SlideShare copy of API 650 (2009, 11th ed. with addendum) shows "10.1 Nameplates" on page 10-1.
(3) An Eng-Tips thread (eng-tips.com/threads/tank-construction-codes.402594/) quotes "10.1.1 A tank made in accordance with this Standard shall be identified by a nameplate similar to that shown in Figure 10-1 ... not less than 4 mm (5/32 in.) high".
(4) Scribd copy scribd.com/document/624967843/API-650, and the blog amarineblog.com/2020/03/16/api-650-storage-tank-nameplate-requirements/, give the same nameplate content (location next to a manhole, names of fabricator and erector).
(5) A 12th edition copy (energy-steel.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/API-650-12th-Edition.pdf) shows the same nameplate wording.

Limitation: I did not see an actual 13th-edition (March 2020) table of contents. Treating 10.1 as unchanged in the 13th edition rests on the section structure staying the same from the 11th through 12th editions, and on my own knowledge of the 13th. Also, a store listing shows a 2025 edition has replaced the 13th. Suggested citation: "API 650 §10.1 (Nameplates), Fig. 10.1".

Several sources agree that the 12th edition (2013) and 13th edition (2020) of API 650 use Section 10 "Marking", with 10.1 "Nameplates", 10.2 "Division of Responsibility" and 10.3 "Certification". I could not open any page directly (WebFetch got DNS errors and curl got a proxy 403), so the evidence below comes from search-result text only.

(1) API's own 12th-edition errata (July 2013, https://www.api.org/~/media/Files/Certification/Monogram-APIQR/0_API-Monogram-APIQR/Advisories-Updates/Addenda-Errata/API_650_12th-Edition_Errata-1_July-2013.pdf) shows the 12th edition places the nameplate information in 10.1.1. It says M.1.6: "the nameplate shall indicate compliance with this Annex by adding 'M' to the information required by 10.1.1", and the maximum design temperature goes "in the space indicated in Figure 10.1".

(2) API's 12th-edition Addendum 2 (https://www.api.org/~/media/files/publications/addenda-and-errata/650_e12%20addendum%202.pdf) lists Section 10 (pages 10-1 to 10-2) among the replaced pages.

(3) A copy of the 13th edition (https://pdfcoffee.com/api-std-650-2020-pdf-free.html, https://reader.assets.udocz.com/uploads/book/raw/656016/api-650-2020-13th-edition-welded-tanks-for-oil-storage.pdf) has 10.1 reading "A tank made in accordance with this Standard shall be identified by a nameplate similar to that shown in Figure 10-1", with letters and numerals not less than 4 mm (5/32 in.) high, and showing API Standard 650, the applicable appendix/annex and the year completed.

(4) Other sources match: an Eng-Tips thread quoting 10.1.1 (https://www.eng-tips.com/threads/tank-construction-codes.402594/), a blog citing para. 10.1 (https://amarineblog.com/2020/03/16/api-650-storage-tank-nameplate-requirements/), and a table-of-contents snippet listing "Marking, Nameplates, Division of Responsibility, Certification". The 2007 11th edition (law.resource.org) already used the same Section 10 numbering.

LENS CAVEAT: 10.1 covers a nameplate being fitted (10.1.1). It also sets minimum 4 mm lettering, which supports legibility, and says where and how the plate is attached: on the shell next to a manhole or on the manhole reinforcing plate, continuously welded or brazed, made of corrosion-resistant metal. It does not explicitly say "not painted over". That part is good inspection practice that follows from the legibility intent, not quoted code text. Citing 10.1 beside "Nameplate fitted, legible" is accurate; the "not painted over" wording should be treated as practice.

EDITION NOTE: a 14th edition (August 2025) is now listed as current. I did not check its numbering, so the claim is confirmed only for the 12th and 13th editions.

clauses.claim: ASME B31.3 para 341.3.3 (Defective Components and Workmanship) requires defects to be repaired/replaced and the repaired item re-examined by the same methods/extent as originally required

votes.evidence:
The paragraph number and title check out. Several secondary sources cite B31.3 para. 341.3.3 as "Defective Components and Workmanship". It sits in Chapter VI after 341.3.2 (Acceptance Criteria) and before 341.3.4 (Progressive Sampling for Examination). 341.3.4 itself points back to 341.3.3 for repairing or replacing defective items and re-examining them until they are accepted. I could not load any page directly (eng-tips, AWS forum, asme.org and webflow all failed on DNS or got a proxy 403), so this comes from search-result summaries, checked against my own knowledge of the code.

Sources:
- AWS forum (https://app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=92399 and tid=22089) quotes the older wording: "An examined item with one or more defects (imperfections of a type or magnitude exceeding the acceptance criteria of this Code) shall be repaired or replaced; and the new work shall be reexamined by the same methods, to the same extent, and by the same acceptance criteria as required for the original work."
- Eng-Tips (https://eng-tips.com/threads/asme-b31-3-nde.426991, a thread from about 2017) quotes the newer wording, presumably the 2014/2016 edition onward: "...shall be repaired or replaced. Examination shall be as follows: (a) When the defective item or work is repaired, the repaired portion of the item or work shall be examined. The examination shall use the same methods and acceptance criteria employed for the original examination." Part (b) covers replaced items.
- Interpretation 22-04 (B31.3-2006), cited under 341.3.3: a repair to a fully radiographed girth weld requires the entire weld to be re-examined; a repair to a spot-radiographed weld does not.
- Eng-Tips thread 515545 (2024) and the progressive weld sampling PDF also cite 341.3.3 with this content.
- Becht and the ANSI blog list substantive changes for the 2022 and 2024 editions. Nearby paragraphs changed (341.3.2, Table 341.3.2, 341.3.4, 341.5), but neither source mentions 341.3.3 being renumbered or retitled.

One wording difference matters. In recent editions (about 2016 to 2022), the repaired portion is examined "by the same methods and acceptance criteria employed for the original examination". The phrase "to the same extent" comes from the older wording. The rule still requires a defective item to be repaired or replaced and the repaired work examined again by the original method, so citing it for "Weld repair: NDE repeated, report attached" is correct. The code does not require attaching a report; that part comes from project QA practice.

votes.correction: The number and heading are correct (B31.3 para. 341.3.3, Defective Components and Workmanship), but the summary uses pre-2014 wording. Since the 2014 edition the text is split. (a) If the defective item is repaired, the repaired portion must be examined using the same methods and acceptance criteria as the original examination. (b) If it is replaced, the new item must be examined by any method and acceptance criteria that meet the original requirements. Suggested summary: "Defects shall be repaired or the item replaced; the repaired portion is re-examined using the same methods and acceptance criteria as the original examination." Drop "same extent", which is the 2004–2012 wording. 341.3.3 says nothing about attaching a report, so the "report attached" part of the checkpoint is not supported by this clause.
votes.evidence: All evidence is secondary. Every page fetch (eng-tips, app.aws.org, ndt.net, pdfcoffee, idoc.pub, cstools.asme.org, ANSI preview) was blocked by the proxy (403 / DNS failure), so this relies on quoted text in search-result snippets. (1) Older editions, 2004 and similar (ndt.net "ASME B31.3-2004 341.3.2–341.4.2" PDF and an AWS forum quote at app.aws.org/forum/topic_show.pl?pid=92399): "An examined item with one or more defects (imperfections of a type or magnitude exceeding the acceptance criteria of this Code) shall be repaired or replaced; and the new work shall be reexamined by the same methods, to the same extent, and by the same acceptance criteria as required for the original work." (2) The 2014-edition copy at pdfcoffee.com/asme-b313-2014-ndt-acceptance-pdf-free.html, a matching copy at idoc.pub, and an eng-tips thread (eng-tips.com/threads/asme-b31-3-nde.426991) quote: "341.3.3 Defective Components and Workmanship. Defects (imperfections of a type or magnitude not acceptable by the criteria specified in para. 341.3.2) shall be repaired, or the defective item or work shall be replaced. Examination shall be as follows: (a) When the defective item or work is repaired, the repaired portion of the item or work shall be examined. The examination shall use the same methods and acceptance criteria employed for the original examination... (b) When the defective item or work is replaced, the new item or work used to replace the defective item or work shall be examined. The examination shall use any method and applicable acceptance criteria that meet the requirements for the original examination." An eng-tips post ties this change to TN 13-709. (3) An ASME cstools document (R2411) shows the parallel K341.3.3 with the same repaired-portion wording. (4) Interpretation 22-04 (2006 edition) answered yes, a repair in a fully radiographed weld requires re-examining the whole weld, "see para. 341.3.3"; that rests on the old "same extent" wording. I could not see the 2020, 2022 or 2024 text directly. No snippet suggested renumbering, and 2014 and 2018 copies agree, so the number and heading are very likely current. Conclusion: citing 341.3.3 beside "Weld repair: NDE repeated" is accurate and not misleading. Only the "same extent" wording in the summary should be updated.
